label: Economy SYD ↔ MEL
description: Qantas Classic Reward: economy one-way between Sydney and Melbourne.
caveats: Classic Reward availability required; taxes ~$25.

label: Economy SYD ↔ BNE
description: Qantas Classic Reward: economy one-way Sydney to Brisbane or reverse.
caveats: Classic Reward availability required; taxes ~$30.

label: Economy SYD → London
description: Qantas Classic Reward: economy one-way Sydney to London (LHR) — one of the best-value long-haul economy redemptions.
caveats: Classic Reward availability on QF; taxes/fees ~$350. Allow 11 months lead time.

label: Business SYD → Los Angeles
description: Qantas Classic Reward: Business class one-way Sydney to Los Angeles on QF.
caveats: Classic Reward availability on QF codeshare; taxes/fees ~$280.

label: Business SYD → London
description: Qantas Classic Reward: Business class one-way Sydney to London — Dreamliner or A380.
caveats: Classic Reward availability on QF; taxes/fees ~$350. One of the highest-value redemptions available.

label: Business SYD → Tokyo
description: Qantas Classic Reward: Business class one-way Sydney to Tokyo (NRT/HND) on QF or JL.
caveats: Classic Reward availability on QF or Japan Airlines; taxes/fees ~$250.

label: Business SYD → New York
description: Qantas Classic Reward: Business class one-way Sydney to New York (JFK) via LA on QF.
caveats: Classic Reward availability on QF; taxes/fees ~$400. Book 330 days out.

label: First Class SYD → London
description: Qantas Classic Reward: First class one-way Sydney to London — the holy grail of Australian redemptions.
caveats: Extremely limited availability; taxes/fees ~$400. Requires 330-day lead time and persistence.

label: Economy MEL ↔ SYD
description: Velocity Reward Seat: economy one-way between Melbourne and Sydney on Virgin Australia.
caveats: Reward Seat availability required; taxes ~$20.

label: Economy MEL ↔ BNE
description: Velocity Reward Seat: economy one-way between Melbourne and Brisbane on Virgin Australia.
caveats: Reward Seat availability required; taxes ~$25.

label: Premium Economy MEL → LA
description: Velocity Reward Seat: Premium Economy one-way Melbourne to Los Angeles on Virgin Australia.
caveats: Reward Seat availability on VA international; taxes/fees ~$350.

label: Business MEL → Los Angeles
description: Velocity Reward Seat: Business class one-way Melbourne to Los Angeles on Virgin Australia.
caveats: Reward Seat availability on VA international; taxes/fees ~$350. Excellent value at ~8.8¢/pt.

label: Business MEL → London
description: Velocity Reward Seat: Business class one-way Melbourne to London via a partner airline.
caveats: Partner award availability varies; taxes/fees ~$400.

label: Business MEL → Tokyo on ANA
description: Velocity Reward: Business class one-way Melbourne to Tokyo on ANA — widely considered the best business class product in the sky.
caveats: ANA availability to Tokyo; taxes/fees ~$200. Book exactly 355 days out.

label: Business SIN → Bali
description: KrisFlyer Saver Award: Business class one-way Singapore to Bali on SilkAir — great for positioning via Singapore.
caveats: Saver Award availability on SQ/MI; taxes ~$50.

label: Business SYD → Singapore

label: Business SYD → Tokyo

caveats: Saver Award availability on SQ; taxes/fees ~$250.

label: Business SYD → London
description: KrisFlyer Saver Award: Business class one-way Sydney to London via Singapore on SQ.
caveats: Saver Award availability on SQ; taxes/fees ~$350.

label: Economy SYD → Hong Kong

label: Business SYD → Hong Kong

label: 1 night at a Category 1 hotel
description: Marriott Bonvoy: one free night at a Category 1 property (e.g. Courtyard, Four Points) — solid city hotels globally.
caveats: Peak/off-peak pricing applies; hotel-specific availability required.

label: 1 night at a Category 4 hotel
description: Marriott Bonvoy: one free night at a Category 4 property (e.g. Sheraton, Le Méridien) — good mid-range option.
caveats: Peak/off-peak pricing applies; redemptions in popular cities offer the best value.

label: 1 night at a JW Marriott
description: Marriott Bonvoy: one free night at a Category 6 property (e.g. JW Marriott, W Hotels).
caveats: Peak pricing can push to 70k; check off-peak rates.

label: 1 night at a Ritz-Carlton
description: Marriott Bonvoy: one free night at a Category 7 property (e.g. Ritz-Carlton, St. Regis).
caveats: Peak/off-peak pricing applies. Best value at resort properties in Asia.

label: 1 night in the Maldives
description: Marriott Bonvoy: one free night at a Maldives overwater villa (e.g. W Maldives, St. Regis Bora Bora).
caveats: Availability is tight; book 12+ months out. Still requires flights and transfers.

label: 1 night at a mid-tier Hilton
description: Hilton Honors: one free night at a Category 3–4 property (e.g. DoubleTree, Hilton Garden Inn).
caveats: Hilton uses dynamic pricing — value varies. Best for beach or resort properties.

label: 1 night at a premium Hilton
description: Hilton Honors: one free night at a Category 5–6 property (e.g. Conrad, Curio Collection) in a major city.
caveats: Dynamic pricing means value can vary significantly; Bali and Thailand often deliver best value.

label: 1 night at an InterContinental
description: IHG One Rewards: one free night at an InterContinental or Crowne Plaza in Asia.
caveats: IHG uses dynamic pricing. Asia Pacific properties offer the best points value.
